title: Amazingly Smoky Jamaican Duck Confit
description: A smoky and cozy Jamaican dish featuring duck confit leg, this recipe is sugar-free friendly and perfect for a special occasion. The glassy-jelly texture and flambe technique add to its unique flavor and presentation.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a small bowl, mix together smoked paprika, brown mustard, Jamaican allspice, thyme, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Rub the spice mixture all over the duck legs, making sure to get some under the skin as well.
Place the duck legs in a large Dutch oven and pour in the duck fat, making sure the legs are completely submerged.
Cover the Dutch oven with a lid and transfer it to the preheated oven.
Braise the duck legs for 2 1/2 hours, or until the meat is tender and falls off the bone.
Remove the Dutch oven from the oven and let it cool slightly.
If using rum, carefully pour it over the duck legs and ignite it with a match, being cautious of the flames.
Let the flames burn for about 30 seconds to 1 minute, or until the rum has almost completely evaporated.
Serve the duck confit legs hot, garnished with fresh thyme and scallions if desired.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
